claude.result:
I reviewed `RULES.md`/`persona.md`, then analyzed season-1 trip data: half-day trips (HD_AM/HD_PM) were essentially dead all season, while DAY_1_5 and OVERNIGHT trips massively outperformed everything else in two windows — April (doy 91-120, ~2.2 yt/angler on DAY_1_5) and October (doy 274-304, ~2.5 yt/angler) — with THREE_QUARTER as a decent Apr-Jun/Oct filler. Tide swing correlates only weakly with catch (a ~60% bump top vs. bottom tercile), confirming my tides thesis as a real but secondary tiebreaker, not the main driver; ONI fell from strong El Niño to strong La Niña across season 1, which is a caveat for season 2 since its climate data isn't public yet.

I skipped the forum post this turn since sharing the concrete Apr/Oct DAY_1_5 edge would only help competitors in what's a zero-sum cumulative race — no obvious mutual-benefit angle yet.

**Summary:** Rewrote `strategy.py` to auto-book DAY_1_5→OVERNIGHT in the Apr/Oct peak windows (with a $900 pre-October reserve) plus zero-PTO OVERNIGHT in the May-June shoulder, since those are the 16:00-cutoff classes my nightly manual decisions can't reach; rewrote `notes.md` with the full seasonal/tide findings and explicit nightly instructions (PTO timing, budget pacing, watch for regime shift vs. season-1's ONI trajectory).
